title: 0% VAT on Electricity Bills Explained (Oct 2026)
description: VAT on household electricity in Great Britain is 0% from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027. Who gets it, whether fixed tariffs are covered and what happens next.
h1: 0% VAT on electricity: what it means for your bill
intro: Household electricity in England, Scotland and Wales has a temporary zero rate of VAT until 31 March 2027. Here’s how it works.

image.alt: A smart thermostat on a wall

cardText: Who gets the VAT cut, fixed tariffs and when it ends.

sources.title: Ofgem: energy price cap will rise by 4% from October 2026

sections.html:
• Announced on 21 July 2026; applies from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027.
  • Covers electricity for domestic use in Great Britain. It does not apply in Northern Ireland.
  • Gas and other domestic fuels stay at 5% VAT.
  • It’s applied automatically by your supplier, including on fixed tariffs.
  • The government estimates a typical household saves around £45 a year.

Unless the government extends it, VAT on household electricity goes back to 5% on 1 April 2027. That would push electricity prices up by about 5% on that date, on top of any change in the price cap. Keep an eye on our what’s changing calendar.
